claims.text: The proposed baseline material is an equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy with a single-phase BCC microstructure in the as-cast or solution-treated state.
A controlled post-solution aging treatment can induce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy.
Aging at around 800 °C for several hours is a plausible processing window for producing the intended precipitates.
The aging treatment will produce nanoscale coherent precipitates uniformly distributed within the matrix.
The nanoprecipitates obstruct dislocation motion and thereby produce precipitation strengthening.
The nanoprecipitates promote heterogeneous strain distribution.
Heterogeneous strain distribution delays strain localization.
Particle-matrix interfaces increase distributed strain hardening and thus increase plasticity.
The aged alloy will have higher yield strength than the homogeneous as-cast or solution-treated reference alloy.
The aged alloy will have greater plastic strain than the homogeneous as-cast or solution-treated reference alloy.
The strength-plasticity improvement requires aging parameters that avoid precipitate coarsening or over-aging.
Precipitate coarsening or over-aging could embrittle the alloy.
The beneficial effect is expected at moderate service temperatures.
At very high temperatures, accelerated coarsening may degrade the beneficial effect.
